items.title: Data Format
What file format(s) encode the data?

options.value: Tabular / delimited text (CSV, TSV, XLSX, etc.)
Non-geospatial array-based scientific data container (NetCDF, HDF5, Zarr, etc.)
Georeferenced raster data (GeoTIFF, COG, GRIB, NetCDF, Zarr, etc.)
Georeferenced vector data (points, lines, polygons; GeoPackage, GeoJSON, Shapefile, etc.)

items.title: What is the dataset layout pattern?

options.value: Partitioned dataset (by year, region, taxon, etc.)

items.title: What is the primary unit of data that is to be operated on?
items.description: E.g., 'Each row is a species observation'; 'Each file is a satellite image'.

Features

items.description: E.g., species name, location, date, observer ID, etc.

items.title: Technical Specifications

items.description: Include file sizes, total dataset size, resolution, bit depth, sampling rate, etc.

items.title: Source Data
items.description: Annotation, Collection, Instrumentation, Methods, Preparation This may have secondary questions for derived vs directly collected data, e.g., information about the source data vs collection method information (ex: sensors).

items.title: Annotation
Annotation Types: What types of annotations or labels are included in the dataset (if any)? Select all that apply:

options.value: Categorical labels (e.g. species names or class IDs)
Spatial annotations (e.g. bounding boxes, segmentation masks)

items.title: Annotation Process: How were the annotations generated or obtained? Select all that apply:

options.value: Automatically by an algorithm or sensor

items.title: Annotators (Contributors): Who performed the data annotations? If available, provide a list of annotators (e.g., ORCiDs), or names/versions of automated tools or systems; or other relevant information.
Collection
Collection (Data Source Type): What type(s) of source data were collected or used to generate this dataset?

options.value: Field observations or surveys by humans

items.title: Collection (Source Data / Data Source Citation(s)): If this is a derived dataset, list the original data source(s) used and provide citation/identifier information for each.
items.description: Include: Title / dataset name Persistent identifier (DOI, URL, ARK, w3id, etc.) Relation to this dataset (e.g., Cites, IsDerivedFrom, IsPartOf, References) Publisher / data catalog (if applicable)

items.title: Collection (Curation Rationale): What was the primary rationale for curating or assembling this dataset? Select one:

options.value: Consolidate distributed sources into a unified dataset

items.title: Collection (Part of a Larger Collection): If this dataset part of a larger collection or series, provide the following information:
items.description: Collection/series name Persistent identifier Relationship (IsPartOf, HasPart, IsPublishedIn) Catalog or repository name

items.title: Instrumentation
Instrumentation: Describe the instruments or sensors used to collect the data, including their specifications and configuration.
items.description: Include as applicable: Instrument/sensor name and model Manufacturer Sensor type (e.g., microphone, camera, spectrometer) Key technical specs (resolution, sampling rate, spectral range, dynamic range) Deployment/operational configuration (height, orientation, settings) Calibration procedures Applicable to: bioacoustics, remote sensing, environmental sensors, imaging, lab equipment, etc.

items.title: Methods
Methods (Collection Method Documentation): Describe the methods used to collect or generate the data.
items.description: You may include: Field, laboratory, computational, or remote‑sensing protocols SOPs, manuals, workflow documents Genetic, acoustic, imaging, trait measurement, or phylogenetic inference procedures Links (URL/DOI) to method documentation Deviations or customizations compared to standard methods

items.title: Methods (Spatial Resolution): Select all that apply
Methods (Spatial Extent): Description of geographic coverage (region, bounding box, domain)
Methods (Temporal Resolution): Select all that apply
Methods (Temporal Extent):
items.description: Start date End date (or leave blank if ongoing) Optional description (e.g., “seasonal sampling 2010–2024”)

items.title: Preparation
Preparation: Describe any data preparation, cleaning, transformation, or quality-control steps performed prior to generating the final dataset.
items.description: Include as relevant: Filtering, trimming, or excluding records Merging or harmonizing multiple data sources Manual corrections or expert verification Gap filling, imputation, normalization Feature engineering or deriving new variables Conversion of raw formats (e.g., raw sensor → - calibrated values) Acoustic filtering, image preprocessing, sequence cleaning, trait standardization Software tools, scripts, or pipelines used (with links if available)

items.title: Data Processing
items.description: Correction/Standardization of values, Gaps filled, Labeling/re-labeling, Outlier removal, Splits

items.title: Correction / Standardization of Values
items.description: Describe corrections applied to existing data values, and whether the data values have been standardized in any way.

items.title: Were any of the following standardization or correction steps applied to the dataset?
Gaps Filled
items.description: Describe whether and how gapfilling procedures have been used to replace missing or removed values in the data.

items.title: Were missing values or data gaps filled in the dataset?
If gaps were filled, describe the method(s) used.
items.description: Include interpolation, imputation, or model-based gap-filling approaches.

items.title: Labeling / Relabeling
items.description: Describe any labels or annotations applied to entities in the dataset and the methods used to apply them.

items.title: Were any labeling or relabeling steps applied to the dataset?
If labeling or relabeling was performed, describe the process.
items.description: Include label sources, standardization methods, and alignment with external taxonomies or ontologies.

items.title: Data Filtering and Outlier Removal
items.description: Describe any removals of erroneous or unwanted data values, and how outlier data values were identified and removed.

items.title: Were any outlier removal or filtering procedures applied to the dataset?
If yes, describe the outlier detection and removal methods used.
items.description: Include statistical thresholds, manual review, or algorithmic approaches for outlier removal.

items.title: Splits
items.description: Datasets are often split into training, validation, and/or test subsets. Describe whether and how this was done.

items.title: Has the dataset been split into training, validation, and/or test sets?

options.value: No – users define their own splits

items.title: If splits are provided, describe how they were created.
items.description: Include whether splits were random, stratified, temporal, their proportions, and how data leakage was avoided.

items.title: Data Quality
items.description: Completeness, Consistency, Integrity, Timeliness

items.title: Completeness
items.description: The breadth of a dataset compared to an ideal 100% completion (spatial, temporal, demographic, etc.); important in avoiding bias

items.title: Is this dataset complete (i.e., there are no plans for further updates to this data product)?
Have quality assurance checks been run and have they passed?
What data processing steps have been completed?
Data Quality: Timeliness
items.description: the speed of data release, compared to when an event occurred or measurements were made; requirements will vary depending on the timeframe of the phenomenon (e.g., severe thunderstorms vs. climate change, or disease outbreaks vs. life expectancy trends)

items.title: This dataset is ...
Quality Assurance Issues
items.description: This should also be documented under Guidance and Recommendations.

items.title: Please describe the quality checks that have failed and provide context for downstream users to work with the data as-is or resolve the issues.
Quality Assurance checks not performed
items.description: This should also be documented under Guidance and Recommendations.

items.title: Please explain why quality checks were not performed and provide context for downstream users to work with the data as-is or resolve potential issues.
Describe any known gaps or limitations in the dataset’s completeness.
items.description: Include known spatial, temporal, or content gaps and their potential impact.

items.title: Data Quality: Consistency
items.description: uniformity within the entire dataset or compared with similar data collections; for example, no changes in units or data types over time; item measured against itself or its counterpart in another dataset or database

items.title: Have all units been translated into compatible forms?
Do data follow a controlled vocabulary?
Provide a reference to the controlled vocabulary used.
Describe any known consistency issues or steps taken to ensure consistency.
items.description: Include examples of standardization and any remaining inconsistencies.

items.title: Data Quality: Integrity
items.description: verification that the data remains unchanged from the original; aka data fixity

items.title: Have any quality assurance or peer review procedures been applied to the dataset?
Describe the procedures used to ensure data integrity.
items.description: Include use of checksums, version control, or audit trails to ensure data remains unchanged.

items.title: Timeliness
What is the timeliness of the data?
Describe the time lag between data collection and availability.
items.description: E.g., 'published within 24 hours of collection' or 'released annually'.
